Just as Mercutio's magic takes hold, a silent shift in the air announces Strahd's return. He stands framed in the doorway, his face a mask as icy cold and impassive as ever, yet the tell-tale redness around his eyes betrays the raw edge of his sorrow. His gaze sweeps over the observers—a fleeting, indifferent pass—then falls to the crumpled letter on the floor, the scattered arcane components on his desk, and finally, the familiar, ordered ranks of books on his shelf. Finding everything precisely as he had left it, the Lord of Barovia enters the room, the heavy door thudding shut and the metallic clink of the lock echoing with finality. Turning back, there was a brief, disquieting moment. His red-rimmed eyes, usually so calculating, seem to pierce through the vision's obscuring magic, locking directly onto Widget's. It was as if Strahd saw not merely through the illusion, but deep into the kobold's very soul. A profound chill, cold as a tomb, runs through Widget as their gazes lock, the future vampire's silent scrutiny an intimate, terrifying invasion. Then, as suddenly as it had come, the moment passes. Strahd turns toward the grand fireplace, raising his hand. With a sharp flash, the roaring flames are extinguished, plunging the study into an immediate darkness. The group's eyes adjust instantly, the world losing its vibrant hues as the monochrome sharpness of darkvision click in. They watch as Strahd reaches for the heavy iron poker beside the hearth. The wall behind the fireplace shifts and groans inward, revealing a shadowy passage, its depths obscured by swirling, thick mist. Without hesitation, Strahd steps into the fireplace and through the ethereal vapor, disappearing entirely, and with him, the vision. (edited)
